text.p: Sterling hovered under the morning's 33-month high of 2.5865 marks in late Europe, as rate rise speculation maintained the currency's bullish trend.

U.K. October consumer credit data and M4 figures in the year to October had little impression on trading, though analysts said they confirmed the good health of the British economy and compounded interest rate rise speculation.
U.K. October consumer credit, which was up 856 million sterling, which fell short of the forecast 1.07 billion, was a good indication of the strength of demand in the consumer sector, analysts said.
They also pointed to the weakness of the mark on general speculation that France will increase pressure on Germany to allow the dollar to rise against the mark and other European currencies.
"Sterling is still in an uptrend on the back of a weak mark," said ABN AMRO treasury economist Tony Norfield.
Norfield said the pound would continue its bullish trend against the mark amid growing rate rise speculation and was likely to peak at around 2.60 to 2.62 marks.
At 1647 GMT, sterling was trading just under a pfennig higher at 2.5820/30 marks and $1.6790/00 compared with 2.5734/45 marks and $1.6796/806 at Thursday's close.
